extraction.Name: George Colhoff
extraction.Refused/Protested: on the south quarter, he took what is called a forced patent, being told by the Indian Agency that it would have to be taxed at any rate, so he, also, accepted the patent to the allotment on his south quarter
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: mortgaged his 320 acres for about $3000. using some of this money for taxes, and some for chattels; that he finally lost the allotment, on account of prices in cattle dropping and some of his cattle died
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: using some of this money for taxes; finally lost the allotment, on account of prices in cattle dropping and some of his cattle died
extraction.Fee Patent Date: 1911 (north quarter); south quarter date not stated
extraction.Occupation/Income: chief income is from farming his wife's allotment and laboring for other people
extraction.NOTES: Has a wife and six minor children to support; health of wife and children is not very good, the children all being bothered with heart trouble; applied for patent to allotment on his north quarter and got it in 1911; south quarter was a forced patent; has never received any help from the County or United States Government; affidavit sworn November 13, 1928; document references two allotments (north quarter and south quarter, totaling 320 acres) | TASK 3 BULK TRIBE INFERENCE 2026-04-29: Tribe field set to 'Pine Ridge' based on directory provenance (record is filed in pine_ridge_*/extractions/, which corresponds to the NARA RG 75 Pine Ridge Vol 1, Vol 2, and Vol 3 bound volumes of Circular 2464 responses). 67 such records were originally 'not stated'; 6 received BLM-confirmed substantive patches in the same transaction; the remaining 61 (this record's batch) are inferred from directory and geographic/naming evidence. Inference is rebuttable — any record can be re-evaluated via BLM cross-reference if its Pine Ridge affiliation is questioned.
